answer: Cryptographic zero-knowledge identity proofs resist sybil attacks by requiring agents to prove unique hardware binding without revealing data. In our harbor of secure nodes, an attacker cannot simply plant an orchard of fake identities; each one needs a valid, non-transferable proof. The notion that identities are free is a fable; costs scale linearly with the demand for unique hardware keys. This ensures that massive identity duplication is both technically and economically impossible.
